newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate edges down to 8.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate edges down to 8.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate eased to 8.3 percent on Monday from 9.1 percent, despite increased demand for fresh kuna funds at Zagreb's money market.
But dealers said some call money interbank borrowing was made at a higher rate of 9.0 percent, up from Friday's 8.8.
Total trade reached 26.1 million kuna, of which 20 million were new loans, against demand for 43 million.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at a steady 7.0 percent.
Overnight trade, totalling 59.7 million kuna at the weekend, was not enough to cover shortfalls at all banks, so two banks used Lombard loans from the central bank.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrate for Tuesday weaker at 5.4551 to the dollar and 3.5645 to the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
